message.content:
**Pantone “Sky Blue” – common references**

| # | Pantone Code | Notes |
|---|--------------|-------|
| **A** | **PANTONE 2925 C** | A bright, slightly turquoise‑tinted sky blue used often in fashion & branding. |
| **B** | **PANTONE 289 C** | A lighter, more muted sky blue—closer to classic “light sky.” |
| **C** | **PANTONE 291 C** | Slightly deeper than 2925 C but still very airy; popular in print design. |

> *“Sky blue” isn’t a single fixed hue in the Pantone system—it’s a family of light blues that evoke the clear daytime sky. Depending on your application (print vs digital, coated vs uncoated paper, etc.) you’ll pick the variant that best matches your visual intent.*

If you’re working from a physical swatch book, look under the “Cool Blues” section near the top of the catalog. If you only have a digital reference, try matching the RGB/CMYK values:

* PANTONE 2925 C → R = 0x8E / G = 0xD9 / B = 0xF7  
* PANTONE 289 C   → R = 0x73 / G = 0xAB / B = 0xDA  
* PANTONE 291 C   → R = 0x71 / G = 0xBC / B = 0xFF  

Feel free to let me know which context you’re designing for—I can help narrow it down further!
